description: Guide Deck — a T-money how-to; 5 of 6 points rest on official pages, the blog-only one is left off.
prompt: How do I use a T-money card on the subway and buses?

guide.topic_en: Getting around with a T-money card
guide.summary: Buy, top up and use one transit card for subways, buses and taxis across Korea.

points.title: Buy one at a convenience store
points.detail: GS25, CU and 7-Eleven sell T-money cards at the counter, and so do vending machines in subway stations.

facts.value: sold at convenience stores and station machines

points.title: Top up with cash
points.detail: Ask at the convenience store counter, or use the recharge machine in any subway station. Most machines take cash only.

facts.value: top up at stores and station recharge machines

points.title: Tap in and tap out
points.detail: Tap the reader when you get on and when you get off, on buses too. Tapping out is what gets you the transfer discount.

facts.value: tap on entry and exit; transfer discount needs tap-out

points.title: Transfers within 30 minutes
points.detail: Switch between subway and bus within 30 minutes of tapping out and you pay only the extra distance.

points.title: Get leftover money back
points.detail: Before you fly home, convenience stores can refund the balance left on the card, minus a small fee.

facts.value: balance refunded at convenience stores for a fee

facts.note: not an official source (news, blogs and resellers can't carry a Guide fact alone)
